transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I've been having some issues at my job. I work as a cashier, and lately at the register, I... I just keep getting stuck doing things that don't really fit the moment. 

Like, I'll catch myself tapping the scanner in a specific pattern, or I'll just completely freeze with my hand hovering right over the cash drawer while a customer is standing there waiting for their change. It's frustrating, and it's been happening enough that it actually got me written up last week. So, I figured I needed to come see someone about it.
When you find yourself tapping the scanner or freezing, do you feel like you *must* do these actions to prevent something bad from happening or to relieve a sense of internal tension?

No, it's not like that. I don't feel like I have to do it to stop something bad or anything. It's more like... I just do it. Or I just freeze. There's no real thought or worry behind it, it just happens and then I realize I'm doing it.
Besides the tapping and the freezing, do you ever find yourself making sudden, repetitive sounds or movements that you can't seem to control?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't make any sudden noises or... or have any repetitive movements like you're describing, other than the tapping I mentioned. It's really just the freezing up or the tapping at the register. Nothing else like what you're asking about.
When you find yourself freezing or tapping the scanner, do you ever feel as though you are observing yourself from outside your body or that the world around you feels unreal or dreamlike?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't feel like I'm outside my body or watching myself from above or anything. 

The store feels completely real, just like it always does. It's not a dream... I'm right there in the moment, fully aware of where I am. I just... I'm just stuck doing the tapping or freezing up. So no, nothing like what you're describing.
Have you ever experienced any head injuries, seizures, or been diagnosed with any neurological conditions?
No, nothing like that. I've never had a head injury or a seizure. And I haven't been diagnosed with any... neurological conditions, no. I've been fine in that regard.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter supplements, or using any substances?
No, I'm not taking anything. I don't have any prescriptions, and I don't take any supplements or... or anything over-the-counter either. And I don't use any other substances. Just... nothing at all.
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of tapping and freezing?

I'd say it's been about three months. The voices, and... well, those more clearly out-of-place moments, like the tapping and freezing up at the scanner, they've been happening for about the last three months.
You mentioned 'voices' a moment ago—could you tell me more about what those voices are like?

Well, most days I hear what sounds like a couple of people talking... usually just off to the side of me. Sometimes they'll call my name from the stockroom, or they'll say I rang something up wrong at the register. But... when I turn around to look, there's nobody there. And no one else around me ever hears it.
Have you experienced any distinct periods where your mood was either extremely elevated, irritable, or unusually low and depressed for several days or weeks at a time?

No, not really. I haven't had any times where I felt extremely high or unusually depressed like that. My mood stays pretty even most of the time. I mean, dealing with the voices and everything can be a bit stressful, obviously, but... no, I haven't had any big swings in my mood for days or weeks at a time.
Aside from the voices you hear, do you have any firm beliefs that others around you, perhaps your coworkers or customers, are intentionally trying to trick you, monitor you, or cause you harm?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't feel like anyone is out to get me or trick me. My coworkers are fine, and the customers are just... well, just normal customers. I haven't noticed anyone trying to monitor me or cause any trouble like that. It's really just the voices and the other things I mentioned.
When you hear these voices, do they ever comment on your thoughts or tell you what to do?

No, they don't really do that. They don't... comment on what I'm thinking or give me orders or anything like that. It's more just... like I said, they'll call my name or talk about something I just did at work, like ringing up an item. But they never tell me what to do.

Beyond the voices and the moments where you freeze or tap, have you noticed that you've become less interested in socializing with friends or family, or that your ability to show emotion has decreased?

I mean, I still care about my wife and kids, of course. But... I just don't seem to have the push to do much anymore. Like, I don't really have the drive to call my son at college, or go meet up with my kayak group. I haven't even been working on my little repair projects at home. And I guess... well, when people ask what's wrong or why I'm acting different, I mostly just shrug. I just can't really find much to say to them.
